title: Lines of Hope
provenance: Original RTS AI narrative. Reuses the six existing standalone campaign scenarios and project map previews; no legacy cinematics, dialogue or game recordings.

arcs.title: The Lifeline
arcs.premise: Three perspectives on a coast in crisis. Keep aid moving, restore the coastal picture, and reopen a passage for civilian shipping.

arcs.title: Broken Signals
arcs.premise: Three independent fictional operations linked by one command lesson: isolated forces fail; a working network turns them into a team.

jizan-corridor.title: A Road Through the Silence
jizan-corridor.intro: At dawn, the coastal radar falls silent. Beyond its range, relief trucks wait on a road nobody can promise is safe. Your task is to restore the picture, remove the mobile launchers, and open a route to the port. A destroyed enemy base is not the measure of success. The convoy must arrive.
jizan-corridor.tactics: Scout the radar approach before committing engineers. Build replacement forces while you clear the launchers; the convoy moves only after both threats are resolved.
jizan-corridor.victory: The radar is back online and the relief trucks have reached the port. The coast has a working lifeline again. Across the water, another convoy is preparing to move inland.
jizan-corridor.defeat: The corridor has closed before the relief operation could finish. Regroup, protect the forward base, and clear the launchers before committing the convoy.

hodeidah-lifeline.title: The Return Journey
hodeidah-lifeline.intro: The supplies have reached the coast. Now they must reach the people inland. You take command from the other side of the corridor, where a surveillance sweep is approaching and an evacuation convoy still needs a way home. Disperse your mobile force, protect the deliveries, and keep the return route open.
hodeidah-lifeline.tactics: Move mobile forces out of the surveillance zone early. Keep a reserve along the return route instead of sending every unit with the first convoy.
hodeidah-lifeline.victory: Supplies have moved inland and the evacuation convoy has returned. Keeping a road open demanded more than holding a base. The final operation takes that lesson to the sea.
hodeidah-lifeline.defeat: The relief route could not be held. On the next attempt, disperse before the sweep and reserve an escort for the evacuation convoy.

bab-al-mandab-passage.title: Four Ships at First Light
bab-al-mandab-passage.intro: Four merchant vessels approach the strait. Their crews see the shipping lanes; your command sees gaps in the coastal picture. Build the radar and technology network, survey the sectors, and remove the mobile threats. Hold Passage Control until the last vessel is through. The lifeline ends where the open sea begins.
bab-al-mandab-passage.tactics: Build the required technology while scouting the sectors. Cover separate shipping lanes and keep defenders at Passage Control during the final escalation.
bab-al-mandab-passage.victory: The merchant group has cleared the passage. Roads, ports, and sea lanes now form one lifeline. Campaign complete: the operation succeeded because the people and vessels you protected made it through.
bab-al-mandab-passage.defeat: The passage remains unsafe. Rebuild the coastal picture, protect each shipping lane, and leave enough forces to hold Passage Control.

straits-shield.title: Across the Divide
straits-shield.intro: Orion Group controls the far shore. A straight assault will leave your force stranded between land and sea. Build the branches of your command together: reconnaissance above, mechanized forces ashore, and naval cover along the crossing. The first operation is a lesson in making the whole army matter.
straits-shield.tactics: Develop repair and naval support alongside your land force. Use reconnaissance to choose the crossing before committing the amphibious assault.
straits-shield.victory: The crossing is secured. Your land, air, and naval forces worked as one command. The next operation tests the network that makes that coordination possible.
straits-shield.defeat: The crossing has broken your force apart. Establish repair and sea control before committing to the far shore.

haitan-network.title: Bring the Islands Online
haitan-network.intro: The command network is fragmented across the islands. Obsidian Directorate forces hold the approaches, and the water gate is the only practical route for your amphibious vehicles. Restore the network, secure the crossing, and combine reconnaissance, missiles, aircraft, and ships. Every restored link makes the next move possible.
haitan-network.tactics: Restore the command objectives before the main push. Send amphibious units through the water gate with reconnaissance and supporting fire.
haitan-network.victory: The network is restored and the islands are connected. In the final exercise, a smaller command must keep its own signal alive under sustained pressure.
haitan-network.defeat: The network is still fragmented. Secure the water gate and rebuild supporting forces before sending another isolated group forward.

hezbollah-relay.title: Keep the Signal Alive
hezbollah-relay.intro: A field relay is all that connects your forward teams to their supply base. In this fictional exercise, attacks will arrive before the workshop is secure. Expand the economy, assemble a mixed defense, and keep the signal alive. Only then can you turn the defense into an assault on the opposing command post.
hezbollah-relay.tactics: Build income and the field workshop before the main assault. Mix anti-tank specialists with reconnaissance and keep a defensive reserve at the supply base.
hezbollah-relay.victory: The relay held, the supply base survived, and the opposing command post is down. Campaign complete: a network is only useful when the force behind it can endure.
hezbollah-relay.defeat: The relay operation has failed. Spend first on a sustainable economy and layered defense, then launch the counterattack.
